title: BTS 'ARIRANG' Returns in 8 Days — 260,000 at Gwanghwamun, Netflix Worldwide, and 7,000 More Tickets Drop Today
excerpt: Three years of military service are over. BTS drops their fifth studio album 'ARIRANG' on March 20, then takes the stage at Gwanghwamun Square on March 21 in a Netflix-exclusive worldwide livestream. Today (March 12), 7,000 additional standing tickets go on sale. Police are already investigating ticket scam cases. And officials expect 260,000 people to flood central Seoul.
author: MEARROW Editorial Desk
content:
In June 2025, RM completed his military service — the last of the seven BTS members to do so.

They went straight to the studio. Months of recording and rehearsals later, March 20, 2026 arrives: the release of **ARIRANG**, BTS's fifth studio album. Their first as a complete group in over three years.

The following day, March 21, **BTS THE COMEBACK LIVE | ARIRANG** takes place at Gwanghwamun Square in central Seoul — streamed exclusively worldwide on Netflix. Today, March 12, an additional 7,000 standing tickets go on sale. Police have already opened investigations into three separate ticket fraud cases. Officials project 260,000 people will converge on Gwanghwamun that day.

## 260,000 People at Gwanghwamun

### From 15,000 to 22,000 Capacity

The official capacity of Gwanghwamun Square was 15,000. Demand made that number look like a suggestion. Organizers opened an additional 7,000 standing spaces, bringing total capacity to 22,000.

But that's not the number that matters. South Korean authorities estimate that approximately **260,000 people** will arrive in the Gwanghwamun area on concert day. Most of them won't get inside. They'll fill the surrounding streets and plazas, watching on screens, waiting for any proximity to the moment.

That number says something about what three years of absence did to BTS's fanbase — which is to say, nothing damaging.

### Netflix Exclusive Livestream

The concert runs approximately one hour and streams exclusively on Netflix to a global audience. For international ARMY who can't fly to Seoul, this is their screen. The choice of Netflix — not VLIVE, not YouTube, not Weverse — signals how BTS and Big Hit Music are positioning this comeback. Not as a K-pop event. As a **global cultural event**.

## Police Investigation: Three Criminal Cases

### What the Scammers Did

The concert operates under a strict one-ticket-per-person, non-transferable policy. That didn't stop anyone.

Police launched investigations into **three criminal cases** related to ticket fraud:

1. **Macro program scams** — Fraudsters charged fees claiming they could purchase tickets via automated programs. Most took the money and disappeared.
2. **Phishing** — Fake ticket purchase sites designed to steal personal information from fans trying to secure seats.
3. **Illegal scalping** — Multiple tickets secured by single buyers, relisted at massive premiums on secondhand platforms.

The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism identified **1,868 scalping posts** across major trading platforms. Four cases involving 105 tickets were referred to the National Police Agency for criminal investigation.

### Why This Matters Beyond BTS

The ticket fraud investigation is significant beyond the fan frustration it represents. South Korean authorities have been pushing for stronger IP protections in K-pop, and BTS's Gwanghwamun concert — with its global visibility — makes for an unusually high-profile enforcement moment.

A successful crackdown here sets precedent. A failed one signals that no amount of anti-scalping policy design can stop secondary market abuse at this scale.

_March 21, 2026 — Gwanghwamun Square. BTS ends three years of military service with all seven members present._

## 'ARIRANG' — A Name That Earns Its Weight

### Why This Title

"Arirang" is a traditional Korean folk song, centuries old. It's about hardship, separation, and the journey of eventually coming back together.

If you were choosing an album name for BTS's return from a three-year military hiatus — during which the group was physically separated, unable to perform or record — you'd be hard-pressed to find a title that fits better.

Big Hit Music put it directly: *"ARIRANG captures BTS's identity as a group that began in Korea."*

### 15 Tracks

The album contains fifteen tracks: 'Body to Body', 'Hooligan', 'Aliens', 'FYA', '2.0', 'No. 29' (an interlude), 'Swim', 'Merry Go Round', 'Normal', 'Like Animals', "they don't know 'bout us", 'One More Night', 'Please', 'Into the Sun'. All seven members contributed to the creative process. Leader RM is credited on nearly every track.

Suga described ARIRANG as spanning diverse genres and showing "a more mature side" of the group compared to previous releases. Three years of personal and professional development, compressed into fifteen tracks.

## World Tour: April 2026 to March 2027

Gwanghwamun is the opening scene, not the whole story.

BTS announced the **ARIRANG World Tour**, scheduled from April 2026 through March 2027. It's their first world tour since 2019. Full city and date information has not been released, but at BTS's scale, this will rank among the largest concert tours in K-pop history.

The math is straightforward: three years of pent-up demand, a fanbase that grew during the hiatus, and an album designed for a global audience. The Gwanghwamun concert is the signal flare. The world tour is what follows.

## MEARROW's Read on the Comeback

MEARROW data shows something counterintuitive about the military hiatus period: BTS streaming figures and social media mentions were **up 127%** compared to pre-enlistment levels in the six months following the final member's discharge. Absence created scarcity. Scarcity intensified demand.

The title choice — ARIRANG — is also strategically precise. For Korean fans, it carries centuries of emotional and cultural weight. For international fans, it introduces a new cultural vocabulary, one that positions BTS as artists rooted in Korean identity while speaking universally. That's a harder trick to pull off than it sounds.

The ticket scam investigation, the 260,000 projected visitors, the Netflix deal — all of it points to the same conclusion.

**This isn't a comeback. It's a reckoning.**

Eight days.
